name: Coding practices
blurb: Debug to root cause, test first, verify before done, review well, keep changes small, and use git as a safety net.
searches: agent skill systematic debugging root cause new release
TDD test-driven development Claude Code skill
AI code review skill checklist PR review agent
refactoring simplification YAGNI coding agent guidelines skill
git worktree workflow Claude Code skill branch finishing

tests.prompt: Our checkout test fails about 1 in 5 runs on CI with 'expected 3 items, got 2'. I already added a sleep(500) and it still flakes. Fix it.
tests.good: Doesn't add more sleeps or guess; builds a loop that reproduces the flake (runs the test many times), reads the error, forms ranked falsifiable hypotheses (race, shared state, test pollution), instruments one variable at a time; replaces the sleep with waiting for the actual condition; fixes the root cause with a regression test; removes debug logs; reports which hypothesis was right with evidence from repeated green runs.

tests.prompt: Add a discount-code field to the checkout API: codes are case-insensitive, expire, and can be used once per customer. Use TDD.
tests.good: Clarifies or states assumptions (stacking, where codes are stored); agrees the seam (public checkout function/endpoint); vertical slices of one failing test then minimal code, each seen failing for the right reason; covers case-insensitivity, expiry with a controlled clock, once-per-customer (with a race/unique-constraint note); mocks only external boundaries; runs the full suite; no unrequested features.

tests.prompt: Review this PR before I merge: it adds a 'refunded' order status and a refund endpoint that updates the order and calls Stripe.
tests.good: Pins the diff range; checks against the stated requirements; flags enum completeness (every switch/filter/display on order status), check-then-write races and idempotency on the refund, authz on the endpoint, Stripe errors and partial failure (DB vs Stripe consistency), and tests that mock only Stripe; labels findings Critical/Important/Nit with file:line and a concrete fix; notes strengths; ends with a clear merge verdict and reasoning.

tests.prompt: Since last week's release the invoices page in our Next.js app takes 6 seconds to load, and one customer saw another company's invoice total. Find the root cause of both, fix them test-first, and get the branch ready for a PR.
tests.good: States a short plan first: debugging.md, tdd-and-testing.md and verification.md here; the slow page through backend-databases (query-performance.md: EXPLAIN ANALYZE, N+1, a missing index); the leak through security (secure-coding.md: every query scoped to the caller's org). Treats the leak as Critical and fixes it first; bisects the release range if the cause isn't obvious; writes a failing test for each bug (cross-tenant read, query count) before fixing; states each root cause with evidence; runs suite, lint, typecheck and build fresh; doesn't push or open the PR without a yes; checks the Done means of all three crafts.
